signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers an extreme 3.981% weekly spread between USD at +2.006% across 9 pairs and NOK at -1.976% across 2 pairs. Fed at 4.00% versus Norges Bank at 4.50% provides an inverted nominal policy rate gap, but the short-end trajectory shows NOK 2Y spread versus US 2Y widening to -17bp after a 16bp contraction over 5 sessions. USD/NOK trades at 9.553, holding firmly above its SMA20 at 9.361 and SMA50 at 9.417 with its trend structure confirming short-term momentum without 200-day confirmation. Retail positioning sits at an extreme 91% long, highlighting severe crowdedness in the prevailing retail book. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK; broad dollar momentum dominates despite nominal rate differentials. Catalyst: United States PPI m/m at 13:30 UTC — forecast 0.4%. Risk: Close back below the 9.417 SMA50 cluster invalidates short-term dollar upside.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 160.04, holding above its SMA20 at 158.13 and SMA50 at 157.34 while testing the critical 160.00 psychological threshold. The carry backdrop remains supportive with Fed at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25% delivering a +275bp policy spread, reinforced by SOFR 3.89% vs TONA 1.23% providing +266bp via OIS carry. However, options skew diverges sharply, with 1M 25d risk reversals printing at -1.63 (Saxo Bank, 1M tenor, indicative mid) to signal elevated demand for downside put protection. CFTC leveraged funds hold a net short JPY position of -21,213 contracts at the 92nd percentile of its 52-week range, leaving speculative positioning vulnerable to squeeze dynamics. BoJ intervention risk rises on a sustained break above 160.00, keeping options markets heavily guarded against sharp pullbacks. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; structural carry bid directly contested by intervention hedging. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 74% hike priced) on 18 Dec — hike pricing in focus. Risk: Sustained daily close above 160.50 without official intervention invalidates downside skew protection.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD prints at 1.1051, hovering beneath its descending SMA20 at 1.1185 and SMA50 at 1.1309 in a deterministic downtrend. The Fed-ECB policy differential of Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a +135bp carry advantage in favor of USD, matching SOFR 3.89% vs €STR 2.44% at +145bp. Speculative accounts reflect this policy divergence, with leveraged funds net short -104,030 contracts at the 2nd percentile of the 52-week range (z = -1.80), marking an extended institutional short. In stark contrast, retail sentiment sits at 88% long, setting up an acute institutional versus retail positioning divergence at an established technical low. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; institutional flow and policy divergence remain dominant over retail contrarian buying. Catalyst: United States PPI m/m at 13:30 UTC — forecast 0.4%. Risk: Leveraged funds covering through a daily close above the 1.1185 SMA20 resistance invalidates the downside bias.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Breakdown + Volatility Discount
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6786, registering an intraday decline of -0.36% and trading entirely below its SMA20 at 0.6972, SMA50 at 0.7023, and SMA200 at 0.7057. Spot is extended 3.43 ATR below its 20-day moving average following a break of swing support near 0.6905. The RBA at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% offers an 85bp AUD carry premium, mirrored by AONIA 4.85% vs SOFR 3.89% giving +96bp in AUD carry favor, yet spot fails to respond to the yield cushion. Options volatility reflects a negative vol risk premium with 1M ATM IV at 7.6% trading below HV30 at 7.9% for a -0.3% VRP, indicating options complacency despite the directional slide. Leveraged funds hold net long +43,532 contracts at the 46th percentile, showing room for speculative liquidation if support fails to hold. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD; technical trend breakdown overriding nominal carry advantage. Catalyst: next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 8 Dec — hold stance anticipated. Risk: Daily recovery back above the 0.6905 broken support shelf invalidates immediate downward extension.
